headline: On the translation lens the v5.0 engine is a regression, and a specific, verifiable one: it emits user-facing prose from inside business logic, in Hebrew, composed at runtime with template interpolation — the exact shape our acorn extractor cannot see (`isStringLiteral` requires `node.type==='Literal'`), Guard D's regex cannot match (no backtick alternative at build.py:453), and Guards A and B therefore never evaluate. It then persists that prose in a DB row, which freezes one language into durable state across a 23-language rollout. But its *decision model* is fine and partly better-factored than ours: typed inputs, enum stages, and numeric returns like `smoke_intensity_multiplier: 1.5`. The verdict is therefore surgical — keep the pipeline, delete every `instruction`/`warnings`/`throw new Error("…Hebrew…")` string field, and make the engine emit `{action_code, params}` only. We already have that pattern shipped in `eqmValidity`.
isItSmarter:
WORSE on the output contract; roughly EQUAL on the input contract; NEITHER is smart about locale-formatted time.

(1) OUTPUT — decisively worse. Proposal §4.5: `pipeline.push({ stage: "THE_STALL_WRAP", instruction: `בהגעה ל-71°C יש לעטוף ב-${wrapMaterial}.` , … })` and `throw new Error("חסימת מערכת: נתח עשיר בקולגן דורש בישול ארוך. אין ציוד מתאים.")` and `systemWarnings.push("אזהרה: עישון גבינה ללא צינור עישון קר יגרום להתכה.")`. Ours, app.js:1941-1949: `result = { level:level, okPaths:okPaths, gaps:gaps, fixes:fixes }` where `gaps` is `{kind:'smoker', state:'missing'}` — a code — and the sentence is built only at the render site, app.js:1979-1980: `` const st=g.state==='missing' ? L('חסר','missing') : L('קיים אך לא מספיק','owned but insufficient'); return `<li>${L('דרוש','Requires')}: ${L(lbl[0],lbl[1])} …` `` with `lbl` from `EQM_KIND_HE` (app.js:1754). Ours is statically extractable and Guard-A-covered; theirs is not extractable at all.

(2) This is not theoretical — it is already biting us in exactly this shape. `app.js` has 68 `` L(` `` template-literal call sites. The most safety-critical one, the Cure/botulism scale warning at app.js:2619-2627, is verifiably absent from `lang/_extracted.json` (I enumerated every extracted key containing "Cure" — 5 keys, none is it). So in ru/fr/de/es/it that warning falls through `L`'s dict miss (app.js:8711-8713) and renders the **English** inline argument. `tests/i18n-completeness.spec.ts:56-58` counts such keys as `deferred/v269-prose` and explicitly does not fail. v5.0 would industrialise that hole across every rule, every stage and every telemetry event.

(3) Note the leak *direction*, because it decides whether we catch it. A bare Hebrew literal that reaches the DOM in a non-Hebrew language IS caught by the raw-Hebrew scan in `i18n-completeness.spec.ts`. The `L(template)` shape leaks **English**, not Hebrew — and nothing catches that. So the moment someone dutifully "fixes" v5.0's Hebrew literals by wrapping them in `L(`…`, `…`)`, the leak becomes invisible to our only render-path gate. That is the worst possible outcome and it is the natural thing a developer would do.

(4) INPUT — modestly better than us. `interface MeatInput { category; collagen_level; has_skin; weight_kg }` / `UserEquipment { core_cookers; control_tools; accessories }` are clean typed facts with no presentation mixed in; our `meta` blobs carry display names (`heb`/`eng`) alongside data. And `return { …, smoke_intensity_multiplier: smokeIntensityAdjustment }` is exactly right: a number the UI words, not a sentence the engine words. Credit where due.

(5) TIME FORMATTING — both wrong, they are worse by one degree. Proposal §5.2 formats with `.toLocaleTimeString('he-IL', {hour:'2-digit',minute:'2-digit'})` for every user, then does `scheduleTimeline.sort((a, b) => a.action_start_entry.localeCompare(b.action_start_entry))` — sorting on a *formatted locale string*. We are equally guilty on the hardcoded locale (`app.js:6141 fmtClock` → `'he-IL'`; `app.js:3615 fmtDate` → `'he-IL'`; several `en?'en-US':'he-IL'` binaries), so I will not claim superiority there. We do NOT sort on formatted strings, and that part of the proposal is a correctness bug as well as an i18n bug (12-hour locales, midnight crossings, Arabic-Indic digit shaping — `ar` is position 22 in the frozen queue).

adopt.item: Numeric/enum return values in place of composed sentences — `smoke_intensity_multiplier: 1.5`, `TIME_CONVERSION_FACTOR = 0.12`, `LOSS_OF_ATTR = ["BARK","SMOKE_AROMA"]`
adopt.why: These are the parts of v5.0 that are already translation-safe by construction: the engine returns a number or an enum and the render layer decides the wording. It is the same contract as our `eqmValidity` gaps/fixes and it costs nothing to keep. (Their *values* are uncited and that is another reviewer's problem — the *shape* is right.)
adopt.whereItPlugsIn: app.js `eqmValidity` (1859) → `eqInvPanelHtml` (1970) is the existing seam; the wood/fuel advisory and `deviceOccupancy` notes fed by EQM (O-6) are the natural first consumers. Enum → label goes through an `EQM_KIND_HE`-style table (app.js:1754).

adopt.item: The message catalogue shaped as a plain `{he, en}` sibling-literal object, NOT as `msg(`…`)` call sites
adopt.why: This is the single cheapest structural win I found and it needs verifying-before-designing: `scripts/i18n-extract.mjs` mode-2-generic (lines 384-409) already harvests ANY object literal with sibling `he`/`en` string-literal properties, gated only by the Hebrew-codepoint guard (`HEBREW_RE`) and `DENY_TABLES`. So a catalogue written as `const MSG = { WRAP_AT_TEMP: {he:'…', en:'…'}, … }` enters `lang/_extracted.json` and comes under Guard A with ZERO extractor changes. Written as `msg(`…`)` calls instead, it would be invisible to both the extractor and Guard D (build.py:453 has no backtick alternative).
adopt.whereItPlugsIn: New `const MSG = {…}` in app.js near `L`/`t` (app.js:8694-8714); harvested automatically into `lang/_extracted.json`; covered by Guard A (build.py:471-507) on the next build with no tooling work.

adapt.item: The stage/pipeline record `{stage, chamber_temp, target_internal, duration, required_accessories}`
adapt.whatMustChange: Delete every `instruction:` and `warnings: string[]` field. `{stage:'THE_STALL_WRAP', instruction:`בהגעה ל-71°C יש לעטוף ב-${wrapMaterial}.`}` becomes `{stage:'THE_STALL_WRAP', action:'WRAP_AT_TEMP', params:{tempC:71, material:'BUTCHER_PAPER'}}`. Also: `required_accessories:['HEAT_GLOVES', wrapMaterial]` must resolve against our 27-token equipment vocabulary from `equipment_map.py` (it maps 1:1 to `EQUIP_CATS`+`EQUIP_OTHER_ITEMS`), not invent a parallel English token set that then needs its own translation table.
adapt.why: The record is otherwise a good shape and close to our `itemStages`/`deriveRequires` output. The `instruction` field is the whole problem: it is the only member that is prose, and it is the member that makes the record untranslatable and unstoreable.

adapt.item: `throw new Error("חסימת מערכת: …")` × 3 sites in §4.5, and `throw new Error(`חסימת נפח: אין מקום עבור [${item.name}].`)` in §5.2
adapt.whatMustChange: Throw a typed error carrying a non-localized code plus a params bag — `throw new EngineBlock('BLOCK_NO_LONG_COOK_DEVICE', {})`, `EngineBlock('BLOCK_SMOKER_NO_PROBE')`, `EngineBlock('BLOCK_BATH_CAPACITY', {neededL, capacityL})`, `EngineBlock('BLOCK_NO_SPACE', {itemKey})`. The catch site localizes. Note `item.name` must be an item KEY, not a display name — a display name interpolated into an error string is a second, nested translation problem.
adapt.why: An exception message is user-facing text here (it is what blocks the cook), so it inherits every constraint a UI string has. We already have this exact pattern working: `eqmValidity` never throws prose, it returns `{level:'uncookable', gaps:[{kind:'bath', state:'missing'}]}` and app.js:2066/2075 turns that into `L('לא נוסף — חסר ','Not added — missing ')+L(lbl[0],lbl[1])`.

adapt.item: Parameterized message templates in general — the `{tempC}` / `{material}` convention
adapt.whatMustChange: A new build-time Guard E MUST land in the same release, before the first parameterized message ships. Reason, verified: `build.py:586` reads `if not a: return True   # source carries NO number → nothing to preserve`. Pull the number out of the string into a param and the source has no digit, so `_gb_safe` returns True unconditionally — **Guard B silently switches itself off for exactly the strings that carry safety numbers**. Guard E must assert (a) the multiset of `{name}` tokens is identical in source and translation, and (b) the unit glyph adjacent to each numeric placeholder survives its `_GB_UNIT_CLASS` family (`{tempC}°C` must not become `{tempC}°F`).
adapt.why: Parameterizing is the right design and it is also a guard downgrade that produces GREEN builds while doing it. `lang/_extracted.json` currently has 0 keys containing any placeholder token and 55 of 1535 containing a digit — so today Guard B's real teeth are those 55 keys, and a naive migration would take that toward zero. This is the highest-leverage single item in my whole review.

adapt.item: Backward scheduling (§5.2) — genuinely useful, and something we do not have
adapt.whatMustChange: The engine returns `{startMs, wrapMs, endMs, restMin}` as epoch numbers. All `toLocaleTimeString('he-IL', …)` moves to the render layer and takes the active locale from `getLang()`. `sort((a,b)=>a.action_start_entry.localeCompare(b.action_start_entry))` becomes a numeric sort on `startMs`.
adapt.why: The algorithm is sound; only the presentation coupling is broken. And the string-sort is a latent correctness bug independent of language.

adapt.item: The two-layer split in §1.3 (authoritative data constants vs. logic)
adapt.whatMustChange: Restate it as an enforceable boundary rule rather than a description: *no user-facing sentence may originate below the render layer*. Back it with a lint — a build-time check that the engine module's source contains no Hebrew codepoint at all.
adapt.why: The proposal states the principle and then violates it in its own reference implementation (§4.5 is the Logic Layer and it is full of Hebrew prose). A Hebrew-codepoint lint over the engine module is trivially cheap and makes the violation impossible rather than discouraged.

reject.item: Persisting rendered prose in the database: `live_timeline.items[].next_action.instruction` (§9.3 / §6.2-6.3)
reject.defect: This freezes one language into durable state, permanently, per event row. There is no re-render path: `applyLang()` (app.js:8748-8758) repaints by re-running the generators — `_mkMethodRepaint()`, `restoreHe()`, `tnode()`, resetting `_mtDone=0` then `hydrateMT()` — all of which operate on strings the CLIENT composed this session. A sentence that arrived as a DB value is outside every one of those mechanisms. Worse, it is written by an Edge Function and fed to `trigger_push_notification`, so a mangled safety number can reach a push notification with no gate whatsoever: Guards A/B/C run in `build.py` over `lang/*.json` at build time and can never see a runtime DB row.
reject.evidence: Proposal §9.3 `live_timeline JSONB NOT NULL` + §6.3 'שמירת JSONB → trigger_push_notification'. Against build.py:471 (Guard A scope = `_extracted` × `_active_langs`), build.py:601-609 (Guard B same scope), and app.js:8748-8758 (`applyLang` = regenerate, not re-read). Store `{action_code, params}` and render at read time; the JSONB column is fine, the prose inside it is not.

reject.item: Running the rules engine — and therefore its string generation — on a Cloudflare Worker (§9.2: 'Cloudflare Worker = מנוע החוקים v5.0')
reject.defect: None of our i18n machinery exists server-side. `L()`, `t()`, `getLang()`, `I18N_DICTS`, `getDict()` are all app.js browser code; `I18N_DICTS_JSON` is inlined into `dist/index.html` at build time (build.py:646-647). Our Worker is a 91-line thin Gemini proxy with zero i18n surface. Moving prose generation there puts user-facing text permanently outside the build guards AND outside the client's language state, and would require shipping a second copy of the dictionary to the Worker plus a second numeric guard — two more things to drift.
reject.evidence: `worker/index.js` (91 lines: `json()`, `export default { async fetch }`, `fetch(GEMINI_BASE + …)`), and OUR-SYSTEM-BRIEF §5's own claim that it 'does not run culinary logic', which I verified. A code-emitting engine on the Worker is defensible; a prose-emitting one is not.

reject.item: `.toLocaleTimeString('he-IL', …)` used as both display format and sort key (§5.2, lines 460-467)
reject.defect: Hardcoded Hebrew locale for all 23 languages, and `localeCompare` on the FORMATTED string as the schedule's ordering. The sort is wrong under any 12-hour locale, wrong across midnight, and fragile under Arabic-Indic digit shaping (`ar` is queued at position 22).
reject.evidence: Proposal: `action_start_entry: cookStartTime.toLocaleTimeString('he-IL', {hour:'2-digit',minute:'2-digit'})` then `scheduleTimeline.sort((a, b) => a.action_start_entry.localeCompare(b.action_start_entry))`. Honest caveat: we hardcode `'he-IL'` too (app.js:6141 `fmtClock`, app.js:3615 `fmtDate`), so I reject the *sort-on-formatted-string* as strictly worse than us and flag the *hardcoded locale* as a bug we share and should fix on our own side.

reject.item: `systemWarnings: string[]` as the warning channel (§4.5), and the same prose-as-payload shape in §4.4's conversion alerts and §7's flavor-matching rules
reject.defect: An array of finished sentences cannot be deduped, cannot be severity-ranked, cannot be tested by code, and cannot be translated. It is the `instruction` defect repeated in a second channel — easy to miss when reviewing, because it looks like logging rather than UI.
reject.evidence: `systemWarnings.push("אזהרה: עישון גבינה ללא צינור עישון קר יגרום להתכה.")` and `systemWarnings.push("אין גריל/תנור/מבער לקרמליזציה. הזיגוג יוגש קר.")`, returned as `warnings: systemWarnings` to the UI. Must be `[{code:'WARN_CHEESE_NO_SMOKE_TUBE', severity:'warn'}, …]`.

impactOnUs:
If we take the ADAPTed version, here is precisely what changes on my lens.

NEW — `app.js`, next to `L`/`t`/`getDict` (app.js:8686-8714):
• `const MSG = { WRAP_AT_TEMP:{he:'בהגעה ל-{tempC}°C יש לעטוף ב-{material}.', en:'At {tempC}°C, wrap in {material}.'}, BLOCK_NO_LONG_COOK_DEVICE:{…}, WARN_CHEESE_NO_SMOKE_TUBE:{…}, … }` — verified to be auto-harvested by `scripts/i18n-extract.mjs` mode-2-generic (lines 384-409), so it lands in `lang/_extracted.json` and comes under Guard A with no extractor change.
• `function msg(code, params)` — dict lookup keyed on the Hebrew source exactly as `L` does (app.js:8705-8714), then placeholder substitution. Enum params (`{material}`) resolve through a code→`{he,en}` label table in the `EQM_KIND_HE` mould (app.js:1754). Numeric params get `dir="ltr"` island wrapping at substitution time — this is the thing free-composed strings can never do, and it is L13's lesson (18 `dir="ltr"` islands exist in app.js today, all hand-placed).

`build.py`:
• NEW Guard E (placeholder preservation) beside Guard B at build.py:600-616 — mandatory, see the adapt entry: `_gb_safe` returns True for digit-free sources (build.py:586), so Guard B goes vacuous on parameterized strings.
• `_GB_UNIT_CLASS` (build.py:541-565) needs `{tempC}°C`-style forms to still classify, so a `°C`→`°F` swap in a translated template still fails the build.
• Guard D (build.py:452-470) is unaffected — the catalogue adds no `L(`/`t(`/`toast(` call sites — which also means Guard D gives it no protection. Guard A + Guard E carry it.

`tests/i18n-completeness.spec.ts`:
• Lines 56-58 currently bucket non-extracted keys as `deferred++` / `v269-prose` and pass. Engine-sourced keys must move to the hard-fail bucket. Expect this to go RED on the first run — that is the RED we want under DoD-2.

`equipment.js` / `equipment_map.py`:
• `required_accessories` must be expressed in the existing 27-token vocabulary (`EQUIP_CATS`+`EQUIP_OTHER_ITEMS`), consumed via `deriveRequires` / `EQM.ownership`. Do not introduce `BUTCHER_PAPER`/`FOIL`/`SMOKE_TUBE` as a parallel English token set — that creates a second label table to translate.

`lang/*.json` × 23 (queue frozen at `scratch/translate-bulk/run-queue.mjs:57`, `it, pt, el, ja, ko, th, nl, hu, pl, ro, vi, hi, id, ru, uk, da, fi, nb, tr, sv, cs, ar, zh`):
• +~40-60 keys for the v5.0 rule/stage/telemetry message set, on top of the current 1535. Each must pass Guard A (present + ≠ source), Guard B/E, Guard C.

DEBT THIS FORCES INTO THE OPEN — and it is owed regardless of v5.0:
• The 68 existing `` L(` `` sites in app.js. Once `MSG`+Guard E exist, there is no principled reason to leave them, and the completeness test's `deferred` bucket is exactly their hiding place. The Cure/botulism warning (app.js:2619-2627) should be the first one migrated on safety grounds alone — it currently renders English in ru.
• `fmtClock` (app.js:6141) and `fmtDate` (app.js:3615) hardcode `'he-IL'`. Any schedule feature makes that user-visible in 23 languages.
• F-8 in `docs/analysis/2026-07-27-gap-closing-BIG-STATUS.md`: the whole-body `MutationObserver` at app.js:11539 re-runs `applyI18n`+`tnode`+`hydrateMT` on a 50ms debounce for every DOM mutation when `lang!=='he'`. A telemetry-driven timeline that repaints per minute multiplies that cost directly.

risks.risk: The engine ships before the message layer, on the reasonable-sounding argument that 'we'll wrap the strings in L() afterwards'. That reintroduces the v274-v277 leak class at industrial scale AND in its invisible form: `L(template)` leaks ENGLISH, which the raw-Hebrew DOM scan in tests/i18n-completeness.spec.ts does not catch, and which the extractor/Guard A/Guard B/Guard D all structurally cannot see.
risks.mitigation: Hard sequencing: `MSG` + `msg()` + Guard E land and are green BEFORE the first engine rule is written. Add a build-time lint asserting the engine module's source contains zero Hebrew codepoints — the violation then cannot compile rather than merely being discouraged.

risks.risk: Guard B silently downgrades itself. Parameterizing numbers out of message strings makes `_gb_safe` (build.py:584-598) return True unconditionally via `if not a: return True` at line 586. Builds stay green, the numeric-safety gate stops gating, and nobody notices because there is no signal — this is the failure mode our own memory calls 'verify rendered, not the metric'.
risks.mitigation: Guard E is not optional and not a follow-up. Additionally: assert a floor — the count of guard-constrained keys must never DECREASE across a release (today: 55 of 1535 carry a digit). A drop is the signature of exactly this downgrade.

risks.risk: Prose persisted into `live_timeline` JSONB becomes migration debt the moment a second language user creates an event. Unlike a client-side string, a DB row cannot be re-rendered by `applyLang()`.
risks.mitigation: Do not ship a prose column at all. If the JSONB timeline lands, its schema must be `{action_code, params}` from day one — this costs nothing now and is a data migration later.

risks.risk: RTL/bidi on generated sentences. `ar` is position 22 in the frozen queue; `he` is the source. A number or `≥` interpolated into a free-composed RTL sentence flips visually (L13). A render layer cannot retrofit `dir="ltr"` islands into a string it did not compose.
risks.mitigation: `msg()` wraps numeric params in `dir="ltr"` islands at substitution time — only possible because the params arrive separately. This is an argument FOR the typed-code design, not merely a mitigation.

risks.risk: Translation cost/latency blowup on the MT fallback path. `mtTranslate` caches on `lang+mtHash(src)` and caps at 3000 entries (app.js:8810, 8826). Free-composed sentences are near-unique per (cut × temp × material × device), so hit rate collapses and each unique sentence costs a Gemini round-trip per language. With `gemMode()==='off'` `mtTranslate` returns the Hebrew source (app.js:8824) — i.e. a Hebrew leak for a keyless user.
risks.mitigation: A finite `MSG` catalogue is pre-translated into `lang/*.json` and never touches `mtTranslate` at all. This is a further argument for the catalogue over generation.

risks.risk: Live-telemetry repaints multiply the known F-8 cost: app.js:11539 observes `document.body {childList, subtree}` and re-runs `applyI18n`+`tnode`+`hydrateMT` on every mutation batch in non-Hebrew. §6.2's per-minute IoT polling means a full-body TreeWalker + `querySelectorAll('[placeholder],[aria-label],[title]')` + `[data-mt]` sweep every tick, for 22 of 23 languages.
risks.mitigation: Scope the observer to the mutated subtree, or repaint the timeline through an explicit `msg()` call path that does not need the observer at all. Either way, measure before and after on a non-Hebrew locale — F-8's 62%-of-long-tasks figure is the baseline.

costEstimate:
On my lens only (translation infrastructure), under our DoD gate — RED witnessed, GREEN, behavioural DOM assertion, Hebrew check, full 816-test suite green per task:

FOUNDATION — ~3 tasks, small-to-medium. `MSG` catalogue + `msg(code, params)` renderer + enum-label table (1 task); Guard E placeholder preservation in build.py + `_GB_UNIT_CLASS` handling of `{tempC}°C` (1 task, the fiddliest — Guard B's regex table is 25 lines of 23-script unit words and touching it is where false-fails come from); flipping `tests/i18n-completeness.spec.ts`'s `deferred` bucket to a hard failure for engine keys (1 task). The extractor needs NO work — verified that mode-2-generic already harvests `{he,en}` object literals — which removes what I expected to be the largest single cost.

PER-ENGINE-RULE — small each. Every v5.0 rule contributes 1-3 catalogue entries and a code+params emission. ~40-60 entries across §4.1's seven hard rules, §4.2 glaze, §4.3 equipment blocks, §4.4 conversions, §5.2 scheduling, §6.2 telemetry actions.

TRANSLATION — ~900-1400 new dict values (40-60 keys × 23 languages) through the translategemma bulk pipeline, plus Guard A/B/C/E passes and the per-language failed-key triage that `scratch/translate-bulk/*.failed.json` shows is real work, not a button press.

THE DEBT THIS SURFACES — 1 medium phase, and it is owed with or without v5.0: migrating the 68 existing `` L(` `` sites in app.js into the catalogue. The Cure/botulism warning (app.js:2619-2627, currently rendering English in ru) should go first on safety grounds. I would argue for doing this FIRST as the proving ground for `MSG`+Guard E, before a single v5.0 rule is written — it gives us a real RED, a real corpus, and it retires a live defect.

WHAT IT DISPLACES — realistically CP2 (11 tasks, 150 code blocks, approved-pending-owner) or the pt-onward language rollout. It does not displace E4/CP3, which are further out. Note the interaction: shipping more languages while the catalogue is being built means re-translating the migrated strings, so the foundation work argues for a pause at pt rather than after several more languages.
openQuestions: Is the engine allowed to run on the Cloudflare Worker at all? Every user-facing string in this product is validated by Guards A/B/C in `build.py`, which run at build time over `lang/*.json`. A Worker-side engine can emit codes safely, but it can never emit text that any guard has seen. If the answer is 'Worker, and it may emit text', the guard regime is over — that is a spec-level decision, not an implementation one.

Do we pay the v269 debt (68 `L(`template`)` sites, including the Cure/botulism warning currently rendering English in ru) BEFORE the v5.0 work, as its proving ground — or leave it and accept two generations of untranslatable prose coexisting? My recommendation is 'before', but it costs a phase and only the owner can trade it against CP2.

Are you willing to make `tests/i18n-completeness.spec.ts`'s `deferred/v269-prose` bucket a hard failure? It will go RED immediately on the existing 68 sites. That is the honest gate, but it converts a reported number into a blocked build today, not after the migration.

Does anything get persisted server-side at all pre-customer? Today state is LocalStorage. If `live_timeline` JSONB lands, I need the schema to be `{action_code, params}` from the first row — retrofitting it after real events exist is a data migration. Is Supabase actually decided, or still under evaluation?

The language queue is frozen (`run-queue.mjs`, `it, pt, el, …, ar, zh`) and stopped at pt. Do we pause the rollout while the message catalogue is built, so the new keys are translated once rather than twice? Continuing to pt/el/ja first means re-running those languages after the catalogue lands.

Do you want me to also file the two i18n defects I found in OUR code that are independent of this decision — the hardcoded `'he-IL'` in `fmtClock`/`fmtDate` (app.js:6141, 3615), and the Cure warning's English leak — as their own gap entries, or fold them into whatever v5.0 track you approve?
